declaredDivergences.what: OOM failures always set the SDL error ("Out of memory") via the allocation seam; upstream SDL_LoadWAV can surface OOM with a stale/empty error string (its decoders return false on a NULL allocation without setting one)
declaredDivergences.why: the #529-B contract requires every failure path to set the SDL error; strictly more informative, never changes success/failure

declaredDivergences.what: IO positions clamp to this ILP32 libc's 31-bit long (fseek/ftell): a WAV needing seeks past 2 GiB fails its seek loudly instead of decoding; upstream on 64-bit hosts can address larger files. size_t is 32-bit, so the upstream size/overflow guards fire earlier here — on the same "WAVE file too big" error paths
declaredDivergences.why: wasm32 address space could not hold such a decode anyway; failure stays loud and named

declaredDivergences.what: IO-layer error strings are this adapter's own ("Couldn't open %s", SDL_InvalidParamError("path")); upstream's come from SDL_IOFromFile with platform errno text
declaredDivergences.why: the IO layer is the one replaced scaffolding layer; decoder-level error strings remain upstream-verbatim (the differential suite compares them exactly)

declaredDivergences.what: upstream's WaveReadFormat leaks its const-mem IO stream on ReadU16/U32 failure paths; preserved verbatim — the paths are unreachable (the caller guards chunk->size >= 14 and every guarded read fits)
declaredDivergences.why: adaptation boundary: no upstream decision is rewritten, and the paths cannot execute
